A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same benchmark study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original segmentation experiments on Cityscapes, COCO and PPD, including model comparisons, adaptation experiments and component analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds model comparisons, PEFT experiments, COVID-19 CT segmentation results and an object-size analysis.

M1.justification: The benchmark sampler and five core adaptation procedures are unchanged. Added models and PEFT methods are evaluated alternatives. The SAM decoder modifications in v3 Appendix A.3 already appear in v2 Section 5.5.

E1.justification: v3 adds four-class, one-shot COVID-19 CT segmentation in Appendix A.9 and Table 12, substantially extending evaluation into medical imaging. Cityscapes, COCO and PPD retain their existing tasks.

E2.justification: iBOT and SegFormer join the main comparisons. Component studies add OpenCLIP and Instagram-3B-pretrained MAE variants. Appendix A.2 additionally compares VPT, AdaptFormer, Convpass and BitFit against SVF and LoRA using DINOv2.

E3.justification: Existing splits, augmentation, training budgets and metrics are retained. Added component experiments introduce SegFormer-B0/B5 size comparisons and an OpenCLIP architecture comparison using resolution 1120 for ConvNext-L versus 224 for ViT-B (Section 6.3, Table 2).

E4.justification: v3 expands model-size, pretraining-data, architecture and training-objective analyses, and adds PEFT-family comparisons, a medical-domain robustness study and car-area versus segmentation-performance analysis. Existing SAM, resolution and register analyses are retained and relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions report three fixed seeds and means with standard deviations. v3 Section 6.1 newly explains that cross-dataset scores are averaged within each seed before calculating the mean and standard deviation across seed averages. This adds statistical reporting detail without establishing additional runs.

E6.justification: Matched aggregate and per-dataset scores for the original five models are unchanged. Substantial new results cover added comparators, component studies, PEFT methods, CT segmentation and object-size trends. In the new CT experiment, full fine-tuning yields 57.35 ± 2.14 mIoU for FCN-ResNet50 versus 32.01 ± 4.82 for DINOv2 (Table 12).

T1.justification: The k-shot definition, construction of nk support images and mIoU formula are mathematically unchanged. Neither version presents additional theorem or proof results.

C1.justification: v3 expands the stated benchmark advantages to adaptation without base-class training and naturally imbalanced, fully labeled scenes. Its abstract foregrounds SSL-versus-segmentation-model comparisons and PEFT. The central benchmark contribution and DINOv2/simple-adapter conclusions remain.

C2.justification: v2's favorable interpretation of larger pretraining datasets becomes conditional after mixed OpenCLIP and MAE results. v3 adds explicit leakage concerns, medical-domain applicability limits, model and energy-analysis limitations, and a geometric-bias explanation for object-size effects (Section 6.3.2; Appendices A.9–A.12).

D1.justification: The code footnote changes from 'to be released' to 'is available.' v3 also discloses reuse of one-shot-selected learning rates for higher-shot experiments and adds NVIDIA A100 to the reported hardware. These disclosures do not establish changes to earlier runs.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands to cross-domain FSS, generalized FSS and recent VFM adaptations such as Matcher, SegIC and VRP-SAM. Section 2.2 positions the broad comparative benchmark as complementary to model-specific adaptations. Additional references support the new models, PEFT methods and pretraining analyses.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, with expanded benchmark motivation and explicit criticisms of existing evaluation settings. Related work moves near the beginning, experimental discussion is reorganized, and several existing analyses move into an extensively structured appendix.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a TMLR layout, merges v2 Tables 1–2 into Table 1 and Tables 4–7 into Table 2, and relocates multiple displays. New PEFT, dataset-summary and CT tables, dataset image examples and the car-area plot substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: New SegFormer/iBOT and PEFT comparisons substantially strengthen model-selection evidence. Broader pretraining analyses qualify v2's general scaling conclusion, while CT results expose an important applicability boundary. Sparse CT protocol details and incomplete integration of its contrary ranking into the main conclusion remain weaknesses, but the gains in comparative evidence and scientific interpretation are substantial.
